planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in well-drained, moderately fertile soil in full sun to partial shade; Prostrata's trailing branches root readily where they touch soil, so give it open ground rather than crowding it against upright neighbors.

directions: Prostrata is a low, wide-spreading selection of glossy abelia that stays under two feet tall while its arching, trailing stems reach four to five feet across, making it useful as a bank cover, tall groundcover, or cascading accent over a low wall. Small, white, pink-blushed flowers open in loose clusters from summer into fall along the length of the trailing branches, drawing bees and butterflies over a long season. Because the stems root where they touch damp soil, occasional lifting or trimming keeps the planting within its intended bounds. It shares the drought and heat tolerance of upright abelia selections once established and needs little beyond an annual thinning of old wood.

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in well-drained, moderately fertile soil in full sun to partial shade; Little Lady arose as a naturally occurring mutation of 'Prostrata' and keeps a much tighter, denser mound than its parent.

directions: Little Lady is a dwarf sport of 'Prostrata' distinguished by a dense, mounded habit and unusually showy rose-pink sepals that persist around the small white flowers, giving the plant a long-lasting blush of color even after individual blooms fade. It flowers more heavily than its parent despite the smaller individual bloom size, covering the compact mound from summer through fall. Its tidy, low-growing form suits foundation plantings, rock gardens, and small-space borders where larger abelia cultivars would overwhelm the space. Like other glossy abelias it tolerates heat, humidity, and average garden soil well once established, needing only light shaping after the main flush of bloom.

common_name: White Gem Gardenia (Dwarf Single-Flowered Container Gardenia)

planting.note: Plant container specimens in spring in moist, well-drained, humus-rich, acidic soil in partial shade; White Gem's small stature makes it especially well suited to raised beds, borders, and pots on a shaded patio.

directions: White Gem is a genuinely dwarf gardenia, staying under two feet tall and wide, with glossy dark-green leaves that showcase star-shaped single flowers of six pure white petals surrounding pale yellow centers. The open, single-flower form is less formal than double-flowered gardenias but carries the same intense, sweet fragrance in a much smaller footprint, making it a favorite for containers, low borders, and tight garden spaces where a full-size gardenia would not fit. As with all Gardenia jasminoides, consistently moist, strongly acidic soil is essential, and interveinal yellowing signals a need for chelated iron or acid-forming fertilizer. Its compact size also makes it easier to bring into a bright sheltered spot during any unseasonable cold snap in the northern edge of its range.

planting.note: Plant container specimens in spring in moist, well-drained, humus-rich, acidic soil in partial shade with some direct morning sun to bring out the strongest leaf coloring; Variegata is grown chiefly for its foliage rather than for heavy bloom.

directions: Variegata is a full-size common gardenia grown for its striking foliage, with each glossy leaf irregularly margined and splashed in creamy gold against deep green, giving the shrub year-round visual interest even between bloom cycles. Fragrant double white flowers still appear in spring and summer, though typically in lighter flushes than on green-leaved gardenia selections, since variegation reduces the leaf area available for producing bloom energy. The strong color contrast makes it a good specimen or accent plant against dark evergreen backdrops in a partly shaded border. It needs the same strongly acidic, evenly moist, humus-rich soil as other gardenias, and a bit of morning sun helps keep the variegation vivid rather than washing out to plain green.

planting.note: Plant container specimens in spring in moist, well-drained, humus-rich, acidic soil in full sun to partial shade; ScentAmazing was bred for repeat bloom, so deadheading spent flowers through the season encourages the next flush.

directions: ScentAmazing is a compact, rounded gardenia bred for an unusually intense fragrance carried by six- to eight-petaled single white flowers with a golden throat. Rather than a single spring flush, it produces successive waves of bloom from mid-spring through fall on the same season's growth, giving a much longer window of scent than older gardenia selections. Its tidy two-and-a-half to three-foot habit needs little pruning to stay in bounds, making it a good fit near a patio, entry, or window where the fragrance can be enjoyed at close range. Provide the strongly acidic, evenly moist, humus-rich soil all gardenias need, and watch for interveinal yellowing as a cue to apply chelated iron or acid-forming fertilizer.

common_name: Summer Snow Gardenia (Cold-Hardy Reblooming Double Gardenia)

planting.note: Plant container specimens in spring in moist, well-drained, humus-rich, acidic soil in full sun to partial shade; Summer Snow's cold tolerance extends the gardenia-growing range northward, but it still benefits from a sheltered site at the cold edge of its zones.

directions: Summer Snow is a densely branched, upright gardenia bred primarily for cold tolerance, reportedly shrugging off temperatures near zero degrees Fahrenheit that would damage many older cultivars, while still producing large, fully double, creamy white flowers over four inches across. It blooms in repeated waves from late spring through fall rather than in one short spring flush, giving a much longer season of the classic gardenia fragrance. The upright, densely foliaged habit works well as an informal hedge, screen, or specimen shrub in gardens at the cooler margin of gardenia country. It still requires the strongly acidic, humus-rich, evenly moist soil that all Gardenia jasminoides need, with acid-forming fertilizer during the growing season to prevent iron chlorosis.
